newsitem.title: JAPAN: Aramco naphtha talks to start next week - traders.
newsitem.headline: Aramco naphtha talks to start next week - traders.

text.p: State-owned oil firm Saudi Aramco and its naphtha customers will hold term price negotiations for 1997 in London next week, traders said on Friday.
About a dozen trading houses and petrochemical end-users from Japan and South Korea, as well as several Western traders, are expected to take part in the talks, they said.
In the initial round of bidding, which Aramco closed earlier this month, Japanese firms suggested prices of about $4.50 above the Aramco formula for Ras Tanura A-180, they said.
A-180 is paraffinic naphtha favoured among petrochemical firms as feedstock for ethylene production.
Currently, the premium is set at $3.40 for the second half of 1996, and at $4.00 for an annual term from August.

The new premium for A-180 is expected to set the tone for the following price reviews for 1997 with other Middle Eastern naphtha producers and Southeast Asian exporters, traders said. Last spring, the premium for Kuwaiti term naphtha cargoes was raised by $1.90 to $7.90 over the mean of Middle Eastern quotes, and the premium for Abu Dhabi naphtha by $1.80 to $6.80, after Aramco succeeded in raising its A-180 naphtha premium by $1.00 to $3.40, they said.

The new price for Saudi Arabian naphtha cargoes is expected to be set by the end of October, they added. Japan and South Korea import about 2.2 to 2.5 million tonnes of A-180 a year on a term basis, traders said.
